A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlowNIB research despite the changed title and framing. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison, including equations, figures, benchmark tables, ablations and implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning results, mutual-information measurements, dimensionality ablations, CPU profiling and single-token prediction comparisons.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised mutual-information results in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The two-critic scheduled objective, normalized loss in Appendix B, Algorithm 1 and single-token prediction framework are retained. v1 already estimates layer information after fine-tuning. v3's frozen-cache description and formalized coordinate selection clarify the existing framework without establishing a different underlying model-training algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same nine classification and six regression tasks, plus ETTh1 forecasting scenarios in the appendices. No dataset, domain or task coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: The benchmark, LoRA and PredGen comparator sets remain unchanged. However, Figure 4 reassigns its reported comparisons: SICK now uses DeBERTa-base/MobileLLM-350M, while CoLA uses DeBERTa-v3-Large/MobileLLM-600M, reversing v1's dataset assignments. The panel image is unchanged; this establishes revised comparison attribution, not newly run experiments.

E3.justification: v3 explicitly defines the reported OIC through a weighted maximum over estimator steps and states that effective-dimension normalization is for optimization rather than reporting. This revises the specified MI measurement protocol. Downstream metrics and tabulated training settings remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The schedule, effective-dimensionality and output-complexity ablations are retained, as are token-level analyses, ETTh1 horizon plots, CPU profiling and the PredGen comparison. Matching the figures across relocation and renumbering reveals no added analysis or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions state that random seeds are fixed. Neither adds numerical seed values, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Figure 3 substantially changes MI magnitudes and some rankings. For example, v1 places DeBERTa-v3-Base below GPT-2 Medium in SST-2 input-representation MI, whereas v3 places it above. Benchmark, LoRA, PredGen and profiling table values remain unchanged. The revised MI/OIC estimates do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the valid-information-plane definition and introduces a formal OIC definition. The consistency result is retained and refined in Appendix B.1 with finiteness assumptions and optimal critics unique only up to additive constants. Several other results disappear, including convergence and optimal-compression guarantees. Retained Appendix A derivations also lose integral symbols.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift from dynamic bottleneck estimation explaining learning and compression toward a lightweight post-hoc framework jointly measuring layer-input and layer-target information. Estimator consistency and the single-token adaptation lose their previous prominence as headline contributions. The central empirical claim favoring bidirectional models remains.

C2.justification: v3 interprets trajectories as estimator training over frozen representations, emphasizes relative neural lower bounds rather than absolute MI, and makes fitting/compression patterns diagnostic rather than necessary. It expands the explanation of normalization and label-space complexity, while removing v1's dedicated limitations discussion, including the explicit scalability qualification.

D1.justification: v3 adds fixed-activation caching, matched critic configurations, shuffled marginal pairs, batch size 128, 2000 estimator steps and default decay 0.001. It also states that no additional noise or quantization is used. These are expanded disclosures; hardware, software versions, hyperparameter tables and the code-access pointer remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The introduction adds positioning against LM information-theory work on explanation, attribution, in-context learning and pruning, citing Fan, Jiang, Wang, Wu and Yang, plus Madiman and Tetali. Donsker–Varadhan and Martin–Masreliez references disappear. The established IB/MINE related-work discussion remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and methodological narrative are extensively rewritten. MIC terminology becomes OIC, ablations receive numbered subsections, the limitations section disappears, the contents move, and an LLM-writing-assistance disclosure is added. These changes substantially reorganize the paper beyond routine copyediting.

P2.justification: Figure 3 changes from four model-grouped panels to dataset-grouped comparisons with architecture hatching. The main-text token heatmap moves to the appendix as Figure 8. Tables 2 and 3 occupy separate pages, captions and floats are rearranged throughout, and the document adopts a different heading and page-layout style.

improvement.justification: The explicit OIC definition, post-hoc explanation, lower-bound caveats and corrected optimal-critic statement improve precision. Removing v1's optimal-compression guarantee also avoids a claim unsupported by its stated maximization objective. These gains are limited by retained encoder-update and normalization inconsistencies, removed scalability caveats and newly missing integral signs in Appendix A.
